title: A Protocol for Revealing Oral Neutrophil Heterogeneity by Single-Cell Immune Profiling in Human Saliva
protocol: Label sterile 50 mL centrifuge tubes for collection of oral rinse.
Set the centrifuge to room temperature (RT).
Have each donor clean their oral cavity and wait for 3 min before collecting the first oral rinse.

Instruct each donor to rinse their oral cavity five times with ~10 mL of 0.9 % NaCl solution (sterile) for 30-60 seconds each time, with a gap of 3 minutes between each rinse to collect a total volume of 50 mL.
Pellet down the cells by centrifuging at 160 x g at RT for 5-10 min.
Pass the cell suspension through a 40 µm sterile cell strainer if there is high mucus content in the sample, before centrifugation.
Discard 40 mL of supernatant from 50 mL total volume by aspirating carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend cells in the remaining ~10 mL of 0.9% saline solution.
Pass resuspended cells through a 40 µm sterile cell strainer using gravity flow to remove food particles or mucus.
Filter the 40 µm filtered oral rinse through pluriStrainer nylon mesh filters, first with a 20 µm filter and then with a 10 µm filter.
Check under an optical microscope after each filtration process to ensure removal of larger cells and food particles.
If necessary, repeat the filtration steps.
Filter the cell suspension using gravity flow or centrifuge at 160 x g at room temperature for 1 min during each filtration step.
Avoid using vacuum suction during filtration.
Check cell viability and density after each filtration step by staining a 10 µL aliquot of filtered cell suspension with trypan blue (10 µl) and loading into Countess cell counting chamber slides.
Use the Countess automated cell counter to count cells and check for viability and density.
Verify the purity and viability of enriched saliva neutrophils by optical microscopy and trypan blue exclusion method before proceeding with FACS sorting.
Proceed immediately to downstream experimental steps requiring unfixed cells or fix cells using 4% PFA for downstream experiments requiring fixed cells.
Prepare the desired volume of lysis buffer in a 1.5-ml Eppendorf tube, adding reagents as specified and placing it on ice before each experiment.
Add 2 μL of lysis/FACS sort buffer to each well in the 384-well thin-walled PCR plate, except for NTC-control wells.
Maintain plates with added lysis buffer at 4°C using chill blocks.
Prepare the FACS instrument with a 100/130-micron nozzle size for daily setup and testing.
Optimize droplet delay for accurate sorting according to manufacturer instructions.
Set up the gating strategy in FACSDiva software for doublet discrimination.
Load a small sample into the instrument to confirm set gating, adjusting gates as needed.
Adjust voltage of the instrument for each channel if necessary.
Confirm FACS setting parameters by targeting the plate with 10-μm yellow fluorescent polystyrene microspheres.
Observe under a fluorescent microscope to ensure accurate targeting and achieve at least 95% single microsphere sorting accuracy.
Practice sorting with single microspheres before proceeding with actual sort day.
Seal the sorted plates with MicroAmp Thermo-Seal lid.
Proceed immediately with lysis and reverse transcription or freeze the plate on dry ice for storage at -80°C.
Incubate the reaction mix at 72 ℃ for 3 min.
Immediately put the plate on ice after incubation.
Centrifuge the plate at 700 x g for 10 sec at room temperature.
Put the plate back on ice immediately after centrifuging.
Add reagents for RT-reaction as specified to each well containing 2.50 µL of lysed cell soup by adding 3 µL of RT-master mix.
Perform first-strand cDNA synthesis of RT-reaction in Thermocycler.
Incubate at 42 ℃ for 90 min for RT and template-switching.
Cycle through the following steps 10 times:
Incubate at 50 ℃ for 2 min to unfold RNA-secondary structure.
Incubate at 42 ℃ for 2 min to complete RT and template-switching.
Incubate at 70 ℃ for 15 min for final heat inactivation of enzyme.
Hold at 4 ℃ for safe storage.
Run PCR-preamplification reaction in a thermocycler by denaturing at 98 ℃ for 3 min.
Denature at 98 ℃ for 20 min.
Anneal at 67 ℃ for 15 sec.
Extend at 72 ℃ for 6 min.
Perform final extension at 72 ℃ for 5 min.
Hold temperature at 4 ℃ indefinitely.
Store PCR run plate at -20 ℃ for short-term storage or at -80 ℃ for long-term storage.
Using BRAVO protocol, perform the purification of the cDNA synthesis product by adding AMPure XP beads (1:1 ratio) to the RT-reaction mix from above.
Incubate the mix for 5 min at room temperature and then place it on a magnetic rack for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant carefully by pipetting.
Wash the beads twice with 80 % ethanol for 30 sec.
Dry the beads on a magnetic rack for 10 sec.
Elute the biotinylated-cDNA with elution buffer.
Incubate 0.5 µL of Low Tris-EDTA (TE) buffer with the sample for 10 min at room temperature.
Place the mixture on a magnetic rack for 2 min to separate the supernatant.
Collect purified cDNA by transferring the supernatant to a new thin-wall PCR plate.
Seal the plate and store it at -80 ℃.

Perform quality control analysis of the purified cDNA using Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips, PicoGreen dsDNA assay, qRT-PCR for housekeeping genes, and optionally qRT-PCR for cell-type specific gene expression.
Check cDNA library size distribution and quality by Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips on the 2100-Bioanalyzer system for randomly picked samples from the plate following the manufacturer's protocol.
Load undiluted cDNA sample (1.0 μL) onto each of the Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chip.
Run the chip on the 2100-Bioanalyzer system to obtain raw data.
Analyze the sample run data of each chip by 2100 Expert software to obtain the electropherogram.
Quantify dsDNA using Quant-iT PicoGreen dsDNA assay kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Prepare working concentration of PicoGreen solution from stock concentration by diluting with TE-buffer (1X).
Dispense 24.50 μL of diluted PicoGreen solution in each well of a 384 Black flat bottom plate using BioRapTR.
Prepare Lambda (λ) gDNA standard of 10 ng/μL working concentration from the provided stock solution in TE-buffer (1X).
Dilute λ-gDNA to varying concentrations by serial dilution.
Transfer 0.50 µL of purified cDNA samples to each reaction well using Bravo for a final concentration of 1:50 dilution.
Manually load 0.50 µL of Lambda (λ) gDNA standard of varying concentration prepared by serial dilution into the standard wells.
Seal the plate.
Mix the reaction components.
Centrifuge briefly to bring the reaction mix to the bottom.
Incubate for 2-5 min at RT, protecting from light.
Read plates in FlexStation 3 or any available Fluorescent microplate reader using Ex/Em of 480/520 nm.
Plot the RFU-values obtained from each sample well against the standard curve generated from lambda-DNA standards to obtain cDNA concentration for each single-cell well and control wells.
Save the SoftMax Pro software-generated file in .txt format.
Incorporate cDNA concentration for each sample well into the final project template file in .xlsx format.
Dilute the cDNA sample to a 1:10 ratio in a new 384 well FrameStar plate by adding 9 μL Low TE buffer or nuclease free water to 1 μL of cDNA using Bravo.

Prepare the required volume of qRT-PCR master mix as specified in section 2.5.8 for dispensing to each well of the PCR plate by BioRapTR, considering the “dead volume” of BioRapTR while calculating the total required volume of qRT-PCR Master mix.
Dispense 7.50 μL RT-Master mix with BioRPTR using designated Reservoir and Tip to each well.
Using BRAVO, add 2.5 μL of diluted cDNA template for each sample, resulting in a total reaction volume of 10 μL per well.
For NTC-control wells, add 2.5 μL of nuclease-free water.
Load the reaction plate on qRT-PCR machine (QuantStudio 6 Flex Real-Time PCR system).
Run a denaturation step at 95 ℃ for 2 min.
Cycle through 50 cycles of denaturation at 95 ℃ for 10 sec, annealing at 60 ℃ for 30 sec, and hold temperature at 4 ℃ indefinitely.
Analyze the generated raw data using QuantStudio Real Time PCR Software V1.3.
Change the "CT Settings” under “Analysis” to a ‘Threshold' of 0.01 and 'Baseline Start and End' from 2 to 10 respectively.
Apply “Analysis Settings" to obtain the final Ct-values.
Export the Ct-values in .XLS format for incorporation into the final project template file.
Consider samples with Ct-values < 35 as good quality suitable for downstream processes.
Perform qRT-PCR to verify single cell sorted in each well using a Taqman assay or preferred qRT-PCR method targeting the marker gene specific to the target cell.
Record cDNA concentration obtained from PicoGreen assay and ACTB Ct-values for each sample well in an excel project template file.
Select samples with cDNA concentration > 0.3 ng/µL and ACTB Ct-values < 35 as double QC-Pass.
Generate a Hamilton input file (.CSV format) for each library plate of each donor.
Load the Hamilton input file into the VENUS software to run the Hamilton transfer protocol.
Place the desired tips and plates at their designated location set on the protocol before running.
Seal, barcode, and store HitPicked cDNA-library plates at -80°C.
Prepare Illumina Nextera XT library for the HitPicked cDNA library plate using ‘Nextera XT DNA library preparation kit’.
Barcode each sample using ‘Nextera XT index kit Set A and Set D’ following manufacturer’s protocol.
Use 1/8th reaction protocol with 1/8th volume of reagents as mentioned in manufacturers protocol for 96-well reaction plate.
Ensure target DNA quality is 1 ng of input DNA with a 260/280 ratio of 2.0 - 2.2 for Nextera Library preparation.
Prepare ‘Normalized cDNA Library’ plate to obtain 0.2 ng/µL cDNA concentration in all wells before starting the Nextera XT 1/8th reaction protocol.
Thaw cDNA library plate stored at -80°C on a chill block in ice.
Transfer 1 µL of cDNA from each sample well to a new Framestar 384-plate using BRAVO.
Dispense desired volume of low TE-buffer by BioRapTR to obtain 0.2 ng/µL cDNA concentration in each well.
Ensure total volume per well does not exceed 100 µL.
Add 0.625 μl of diluted cDNA (0.2 ng/μL) to the Tagment DNA Buffer and Amplification Tagment Mix in a Framestar 384-well microplate.
Seal the plate, mix by brief centrifuge, and load on the thermocycler for incubation at 55 °C for 10 min.
Add 0.625 μl of NT buffer to neutralize the Tagmentation reaction in each well to obtain a total volume of 3.125 µL.

To the tagmentation volume, add 1.875 μl NPM PCR master mix and 1.250 μl Index Primer mix (0.625 μl Index Primer i5 + 0.625 μl Index Primer i7) to obtain a total volume of 6.25 µL Nextera PCR reaction/well.
Seal the plate, centrifuge at 4 °C, 500 x g (2,000 RPM) for 30 sec to mix, and keep on ice until running the thermocycler reaction.
Denature the sample at 95 °C for 30 sec.
Extend the sample at 72 °C for 3 min.
Denature the sample at 95 °C for 10 sec.
Anneal the sample at 55 °C for 30 sec.
Extend the sample at 72 °C for 60 sec.
Perform final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.
Hold the plate at 4 °C until ready for library purification and cleanup.
Purify each sample individually using a 0.9:1 ratio of AMPure XP beads to Nextera library.
Elute with 6.25 µL of Low TE buffer into a new FrameStar plate labeled "Purified Nextera XT".
Seal the plate and store at -80 °C until ready for PicoGreen QC or normalization of the purified library.
Use 1 µL of the purified Nextera XT reactions for Picogreen dsDNA assay.
Prepare 1.0 ng/µL normalization plate of purified Nextera library based on the PicoGreen quantification.
Dispense the desired amount of Low-TE buffer to a new Framestar plate using BioRaPTR.
Add 1 µL of purified Nextera XT library sample to obtain 1.0 ng/µL purified Nextera XT sample in each well using BRAVO.
Pool 16 NexteraXT samples for MiSeq run.
Pool 16 samples by pipetting 3 μL of all normalized Nextera XT samples into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube.
Reverse pipette to determine the total volume.
Add 90% of that volume AMPure beads to purify the MiSeq-pooled library as in Nextera XT library cleanup.
Elute with Low-TE buffer using 10-fold lower volume than the original volume of pooled library determined by reverse pipetting.
Prepare 1:1 dilution (take out 1 μL) for QC check on Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips.
Prepare 1:10 dilution (1 μL library + 9 μL Low TE) for QC check on Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips.
Prepare 1:20 dilution (2 μL of 1:10 dilution + 2 μL of Low-TE) for QC check on Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips.
Run each of the 3 samples in triplicate on Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chip.
Calculate the average fragment size and the average pool concentration in pmol/L (pM) and nM of all replicates from DNA chip run report.
Store the MiSeq-pooled library at -20 °C until ready for sequencing run.
For each 384-well library plate, combine all 384 normalized Nextera XT libraries from each well to a single well by using BRAVO.
Pipette the 384-plex pool to an Eppendorf tube and label the tube with sample and library name.
Clean the 384-plex pool Nextera XT library using AMPure XP bead purification.
Use 1 µL of the 384-plex pool Nextera XT Library samples to check quality on a Bioanalyzer using Agilent high-sensitivity DNA chips.
Save the Bioanalyzer report for each 384-plex pool library.
Calculate and prepare volumes enough for 3 replicates of NTC, each sample dilution, and each standard.
Prepare four different dilution sets of the pooled Nextera XT library by adding required volume of dilution solution.
Prepare qPCR master mix by combining 1 mL of Illumina Primer Premix (10X) with the 5 mL bottle of KAPA SYBR Fast qPCR master mix (2X).
Vortex briefly to mix well.
Store the qPCR master mix at -20 °C until ready to use.
For half reaction volume, add 6 µL of qPCR master mix and 4 µL of sample or standards to appropriate wells.
Add 4 µL nuclease-free water to NTC (no template control) wells.
Seal the plate.
Gently vortex the sealed plate to mix.
Spin down samples to bottom of the well.
Protect the plate from light until ready to run.
Run the sample plate on QuantStudio 6 Flex or any other qPCR machine by selecting the “Standard Curve” experimental method and “SYBR Green” detector.
Run the instrument in “Fast” mode.
Set the initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min.
Program 35 cycles of denaturation at 95 °C for 20 sec.
Program annealing at 60°C for 45 sec.
Hold the final temperature at 4 °C indefinitely.
Analyze qPCR data upon completion.
Evaluate the Slope and R2.
Plot the average Ct value of each DNA standard against its known concentration (pM) to generate a standard curve.
Use the standard curve to determine the concentration (pM) of diluted libraries.
Combine qPCR amplified product from three replicate wells and run on 1.2% E-Gel for 30 min using 1 kb plus ladder and 6X loading dye.
Verify the quality and fragment size of pooled NexteraXT library samples before proceeding to cDNA sequencing.
Subject purified pooled-NexteraXT library to paired-end sequencing on a suitable Illumina NGS platform to generate 1-2 million reads per sample with a read length of 100-150 bases.
Evaluate fastq sequence files from each cell using the fastQC tool for sequence yield, base quality, GC profile, k-mer distribution, contamination and other parameters.
Calculate the absolute number of identical reads in input sample fastq sequences using tools such as fastx_collapser with correct base quality score offset (-Q).
Process multiple sequence files by repeating each file at a time.
Trim input paired-end fastq reads using Trimmomatic program to remove adapter/primer sequences and low-quality end bases.
Prepare the reference genome index for alignment using the HISAT2 program and the reference genome fasta file.
Calculate the gene expression values (transcripts per million or TPM) by mapping paired-end reads to the reference index using HISAT2.
Evaluate the alignments using StringTie to estimate levels of expression per gene models in the annotation file.
Calculate the number of reads that are mapped to the genome using SAM tools.
Calculate the number of reads mapped to the ERCC spike-in transcripts using SAM tools.
Calculate the number of reads that remained unmapped using SAM tools.
